# OmniCapital — The Application That Could Not Move
> **GitHub-first narrative · GICS07 Financials · 2026-10-19.** Fictional architecture learning case. GitHub is canonical; Notion is the KM hub. New names, incidents and options are illustrative. Original research, HR capability example and14child references remain below. Unattended synchronization is unverified.
**Start here:** [Executive One-Pager](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/07-financials/omnicapital-financial-group-ltd/executive-one-pager.md) · [Hero Story](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/07-financials/omnicapital-financial-group-ltd/hero-story.md) · [22-Section Master](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/07-financials/omnicapital-financial-group-ltd/master/README.md) · [16 Personas](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/07-financials/omnicapital-financial-group-ltd/personas/persona-cards.md) · [12 Simulations](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/07-financials/omnicapital-financial-group-ltd/simulations/README.md) · [Seven Streams](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/07-financials/omnicapital-financial-group-ltd/derived-streams/README.md) · [Resources](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/07-financials/omnicapital-financial-group-ltd/resources/README.md)
## Prologue — An exception without shared ownership
An invented SME customer repeatedly submits a document while service and verification teams show different exception status. This triggers discovery, not a claim about an actual customer or proven cause.
## Act I — Understand the Enterprise (OCF-M01–04)
Fictional CEO **Anika Shah (OCF-P01)** leads a source-stipulated **USD46B** group with **USD1.4T AUM,58M customers and32countries**, headquartered in London/Mumbai.
Revenue mix:retail/digital31%, commercial24%, wealth19%, insurance16%, payments/markets10%. AUM is not revenue, owned assets or cash. Staff and branch counts are not supplied.
Source problems:fragmented data, manual onboarding/service, legacy-core constraints and rising control demands.
[Enterprise theme](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/07-financials/omnicapital-financial-group-ltd/master/theme-a-enterprise.md)
## Act II — Choose the Future (OCF-M05–08)
Customer chief **Priya Rao (OCF-P03)** asks who is excluded; risk chief **Arjun Mehta (OCF-P04)** requires accountability; CFO **David Morgan (OCF-P02)** demands credible value.
Compare product-local pilots, enterprise platform first and federated customer-journey experiments under common controls. Third option is provisional.
Source ambitions NPS\>60,90%digital completion,35%automation and14%ROE improvement lack sufficient definitions/baselines.
[Strategy theme](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/07-financials/omnicapital-financial-group-ltd/master/theme-b-strategy.md)
## Act III — Architect Trusted Financial Journeys (OCF-M09–12)
Source chain: **Acquire → Verify → Advise → Transact → Protect → Grow → Retain**.
Identity lead **Mei Tan (OCF-P09)** and architect **Daniel Weber (OCF-P12)** connect Customer/Account/Transaction/Risk/Product360 to source-proposed core banking, policy admin, CRM, lending, payments, risk engines, APIs and events.
**Omar Haddad (OCF-P10)** requires tested access/recovery;**Dr.Leila Costa (OCF-P13)** requires model purpose, fairness, explanation, monitoring and accountable review. Proposals are not validated systems or regulatory assurance.
[Architecture theme](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/07-financials/omnicapital-financial-group-ltd/master/theme-c-architecture.md)
## Act IV — Fund and Sequence Evidence (OCF-M13–16)
Source proposes **USD780M over3years** and **USD340M annual value**. Components, phasing, incremental costs, overlap, cash conversion and capital effects are absent; NPV/payback remain unvalidated.
Year1 MDM/API/cloud/identity/fraud → Year2 journey/risk-data/automation → Year3 embedded finance, advice and real-time risk proposals.
Targets:Year1 95%identity match/25%digital onboarding; Year2 40%faster onboarding/20%lower service cost; Year3 70%self-service/30%automation.
[Transformation theme](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/07-financials/omnicapital-financial-group-ltd/master/theme-d-transformation.md)
## Act V — Make Change Accountable and Usable (OCF-M17–19)
Compliance lead **Elena Fischer (OCF-P05)** asks who owns unresolved evidence. CHRO **Nadia Fernandes (OCF-P07)** preserves the source's employee-onboarding example while distinguishing it from customer onboarding.
Illustrative first pilot:synthetic-data document intake/exception routing with approved access, identity uncertainty, late/duplicate events, evidence lineage, reconciliation, recovery and rollback. No automated credit, pricing or advice release is included.
[Execution theme](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/07-financials/omnicapital-financial-group-ltd/master/theme-e-execution.md)
## Act VI — Prove Value (OCF-M20–22)
NPS, cost-to-income, fraud loss, onboarding time, model evidence and compliance require owners, baselines, definitions and balancing measures.
**35%versus30%automation** and **90%completion versus70%self-service** remain visible scope/time/definition gaps. Match rate alone does not prove identity assurance. All future figures are targets, not results.
[Value theme](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/07-financials/omnicapital-financial-group-ltd/master/theme-f-value.md)
## Meet the Fictional Stakeholders
Anika Shah—CEO; David Morgan—CFO; Priya Rao—Customer; Arjun Mehta—Risk; Elena Fischer—Compliance; Sofia Chen—Digital/Information; Nadia Fernandes—CHRO; Marcus Okoro—Financial Crime; Mei Tan—Identity/Data; Omar Haddad—Security/Resilience; Grace Menon—Open Finance; Daniel Weber—EA; Dr.Leila Costa—Model Risk/AI; Ravi Patel—Payments/Treasury; Amelia Brooks—SME Customer; Ingrid Sørensen—Procurement/Third Party.
[Authority, objections and withheld evidence](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/07-financials/omnicapital-financial-group-ltd/personas/persona-cards.md)
## Practice and Derive
Twelve simulations cover discovery, identity, funding, financial crime, workforce, open finance, resilience, AI governance, inclusion, third parties, architecture and hypothetical STAR.
Seven scope blueprints cover Workforce/HR, CX, Finance, Procurement, Service Operations/Supply Chain, Business Transformation and Leadership.
**13HR child pages plus one banking-AI reference** are preserved; child bodies unaudited. External media remain planned.
[Scripts](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/07-financials/omnicapital-financial-group-ltd/simulations/scenario-scripts.md) · [Streams](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/07-financials/omnicapital-financial-group-ltd/derived-streams/README.md) · [14 child references](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/07-financials/omnicapital-financial-group-ltd/references/notion-child-cases.md)
## Source and Synchronization Governance
Original research stays protected. Exact narrative is mapped to a GitHub baseline; conflicting edits are held. Other canonical changes require deliberate reconciliation; child pages and attachments are not losslessly mirrored.
[Sources/gaps](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/07-financials/omnicapital-financial-group-ltd/references/source-and-assumptions.md) · [Sync protocol](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/07-financials/omnicapital-financial-group-ltd/sync/README.md) · [Delivery report](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/07-financials/omnicapital-financial-group-ltd/delivery-report-2026-10-19.md)
**Delivery validation:** GitHub-to-Notion narrative was read back successfully. This note originated in Notion for the reverse-transfer test. OmniCapital is registered for daily reconciliation; unattended integration remains unverified.

# 🌟 GICS07. OmniCapital Financial Group Ltd. — Digital Transformation Case Study ## **Company Overview** **OmniCapital Financial Group Ltd.** is a fictional multinational financial-services group spanning retail and commercial banking, insurance, wealth management, payments, and capital-markets services. It is transforming into a trusted, AI-enabled financial ecosystem while strengthening resilience, transparency, and customer outcomes. --- ## **📊 Company Profile**
**Attribute** **Details**
**Founded** 1979
**Headquarters** London, UK & Mumbai, India
**Markets Served** 32 countries
**Annual Revenue** \$46 billion USD
**Assets Under Management** \$1.4 trillion USD
**Customers** 58 million retail, SME, corporate, and wealth clients
### **Business Portfolio**
**Segment** **Revenue %** **Services**
Retail & Digital Banking 31% Deposits, lending, cards, mobile banking
Commercial Banking 24% SME finance, cash management, trade finance
Wealth & Asset Management 19% Advisory, investments, retirement solutions
Insurance 16% Life, health, property, and embedded insurance
Payments & Markets 10% Payment infrastructure, treasury, capital-markets services
--- ## **🎯 Digital Transformation Vision** > *“Creating trusted, intelligent, and inclusive financial experiences through secure platforms, real-time insight, and responsible innovation.”* ### **Transformation Drivers** 1. **Customer Expectation:** instant, personalised, frictionless financial services. 2. **Risk & Regulation:** greater transparency, resilience, financial-crime prevention, and consumer protection. 3. **Cost-to-Serve:** retire fragmented legacy systems and automate high-volume work. 4. **Open Ecosystems:** create secure embedded-finance and partner capabilities. 5. **Sustainable Finance:** integrate climate and social risk into financial decisions. --- # 🏗️ **TOGAF-Aligned Architecture Design** ## **Phase A: Architecture Vision** ### **Current-State Challenges** - Product, customer, risk, and transaction data reside in disconnected platforms. - Onboarding and servicing journeys involve manual review and repeated data entry. - Legacy core systems slow product launches and limit real-time decisioning. - Fraud, cybercrime, model risk, and regulatory obligations require stronger enterprise controls. ### **Stakeholder Outcomes**
**Stakeholder** **Outcome** **Success Measure**
Customers Simple, trusted, personalised finance NPS \>60; 90% digital service completion
Regulators Transparent, resilient, fair conduct 100% timely compliance reporting
Employees Fewer manual controls and better decision tools 35% operations automation
Investors Profitable, risk-adjusted growth 14% ROE improvement
## **Phase B: Business Architecture** ```plain text FINANCIAL VALUE STREAM Acquire → Verify → Advise → Transact → Protect → Grow → Retain Future State: real-time, consent-based, risk-aware financial journeys. ```
**Capability** **Target State** **Digital Enablers**
Customer Onboarding Digital, low-friction, compliant Digital identity, KYC automation, document AI
Credit & Underwriting Fast, explainable, risk-aware Decision engines, responsible ML
Financial Crime Proactive detection and investigation Graph analytics, anomaly detection
Advice & Service Personalised, omni-channel engagement Customer 360, advisor workbench, copilots
Give an example of a business capability from an HR point of view **Example HR business capability (for this use case: “Digital onboarding + automation + responsible AI” in OmniCapital’s transformation):** ### **Capability: “AI-assisted Employee Onboarding & Compliance Readiness”** HR’s ability to **onboard new hires quickly and safely** in a regulated financial-services environment by combining workflow automation, document intelligence, and policy/compliance checks. **What it includes (capability scope):** - **Digital identity & pre-employment verification** (right-to-work, background checks, credential validation) - **Document intake + intelligent processing** (contracts, IDs, certifications, tax/payroll forms) with exception routing to HR ops - **Role-based provisioning** triggers (request accounts, tools, and access based on job family and risk tier) - **Mandatory learning + policy attestation orchestration** (AML, data privacy, cyber hygiene, conduct risk) before system access is granted - **Audit-ready onboarding evidence** (who approved what, when; documentation completeness; training completion) for regulators and internal risk teams **Why it’s specifically relevant here:**
It mirrors the case study’s enterprise pattern—**reduce manual work, improve compliance transparency, and increase speed-to-productivity**—but applied to the workforce, where financial services has strict controls (access, conduct, regulatory training) similar to customer onboarding. **Simple success measures (KPIs):** - Time-to-productivity (days from offer to “fully productive”) - % onboarding completed digitally end-to-end - Compliance completion rate before Day 1 / before access issuance - Exceptions per hire and average exception resolution time - Audit findings related to onboarding/access/training evidence ## **Phase C: Information Systems Architecture** ### **Data Architecture** ```plain text FINANCIAL GOLDEN RECORDS Customer 360° → Account 360° → Transaction 360° → Risk 360° → Product 360° ``` - **Customer data:** consent-managed identity, preferences, relationships, affordability and service history. - **Risk data:** credit, market, liquidity, operational, fraud, and climate-risk data with lineage. - **Transaction data:** real-time events for payments, trades, servicing, and controls. - **Governance:** data quality, retention, explainability, privacy, and model-risk control by design. ### **Target Application Landscape**
**Layer** **Core Systems** **Pattern**
Experience Mobile banking, web, advisor desktop, contact-centre tools Journey-led and omni-channel
Process Core banking, policy admin, CRM, lending, payments, risk engines Domain services and workflow orchestration
Integration Open-banking APIs, iPaaS, event mesh, partner gateway API-first and event-driven
Data Lakehouse, MDM, ledger data, feature store, regulatory platform Governed and lineage-aware data products
## **Phase D: Technology Architecture** - **Hybrid cloud:** regulated core and sensitive ledgers operate in controlled environments; analytics and customer services scale in cloud. - **Resilience by design:** active-active services, tested recovery, observability, and third-party risk controls. - **Zero trust:** customer identity protection, privileged access controls, encryption, and continuous fraud monitoring. --- # 🤖 **AI & Advanced Analytics**
**Use Case** **Business Value** **Approach**
Financial-Crime Detection Faster, more accurate alert prioritisation Graph AI and explainable anomaly detection
Next-Best Financial Action Relevant advice and retention Consent-aware customer analytics
Intelligent Document Processing Shorter onboarding and claims processing Document AI with human exception review
Risk & Treasury Simulation Better stress testing and liquidity decisions Scenario modelling and digital twins
**Responsible AI rule:** no high-impact credit, pricing, fraud, or advice decision is released without fairness testing, explainability, human accountability, and ongoing monitoring. --- # 📊 **3-Year Roadmap & Value Realisation**
**Phase** **Key Initiatives** **Success Metrics**
**Year 1 — Foundation** Customer MDM, API platform, cloud controls, identity and fraud uplift 95% identity match; 25% digital onboarding
**Year 2 — Acceleration** Journey modernisation, risk lakehouse, operations automation 40% faster onboarding; 20% lower service cost
**Year 3 — Transformation** Embedded finance, intelligent advice, real-time risk optimisation 70% digital self-service; 30% operations automation
### **Investment & Outcomes** - **3-year investment:** \$780M in core modernisation, data, cyber resilience, and customer journeys. - **Expected benefits:** \$340M annual value from automation, reduced loss, improved retention, and faster product delivery. - **Core KPIs:** customer NPS, cost-to-income ratio, fraud-loss rate, onboarding time, model performance, and regulatory compliance. --- # 🎉 **Conclusion** **OmniCapital Financial Group Ltd.** becomes a real-time, trusted financial platform that combines personal relevance with disciplined risk management. The transformation succeeds when innovation, customer fairness, resilience, and regulatory accountability move together. --- ## 14. Aligned business transformation case study blueprint ## Alignment purpose This section refines OmniCapital into the same business transformation case study structure used for OmniSpace while preserving the existing content. ### 14.1 Executive case narrative OmniCapital Financial Group Ltd. is transforming from product-led financial services into a real-time, trusted, AI-enabled, risk-aware financial ecosystem. **Core transformation statement:** OmniCapital is not only modernizing banking platforms; it is building a governed financial operating model where customer identity, risk, transactions, products, open APIs, responsible AI, resilience, and value realization work as one system. ### 14.2 Business problem statement
**Problem area** **Current challenge** **Transformation need**
Fragmented customer and risk data Customer, product, transaction, and risk records sit across disconnected platforms. Create Customer 360, Account 360, Transaction 360, Risk 360, and Product 360.
Manual onboarding and servicing KYC, document review, claims, credit, and service work require repeated manual effort. Use digital identity, document AI, workflow automation, and explainable decisioning.
Legacy core constraints Core systems limit real-time experiences and rapid product launches. Modernize through APIs, domain services, cloud controls, and event-driven architecture.
Financial-crime and cyber risk Fraud, cybercrime, and regulatory expectations demand stronger controls. Deploy graph analytics, zero trust, fraud monitoring, and resilient operations.
Responsible AI and conduct Credit, pricing, advice, and fraud AI create fairness and explainability risk. Build model-risk governance, fairness testing, human accountability, and monitoring.
### 14.3 Target transformation operating model ```plain text Business Outcomes ↓ Capability Architecture — Onboarding, lending, payments, advice, risk, protection ↓ Process Architecture — Acquire, verify, advise, transact, protect, grow, retain ↓ Data Architecture — Customer, account, transaction, risk, product golden records ↓ Application Architecture — Core banking, policy admin, CRM, lending, payments, risk ↓ Integration Architecture — Open banking APIs, event mesh, partner gateway ↓ Technology Architecture — Hybrid cloud, resilience, zero trust, AI platforms ↓ Regulatory Governance, Responsible AI, Adoption, and Value Realization ``` **Operating rule:** Every financial workstream must connect customer fairness, regulatory control, risk data, digital journey, resilience, model governance, adoption, and measurable value. ### 14.4 Workstream alignment map
**Workstream** **Business outcome** **Architecture / process focus** **Delivery and adoption focus**
Digital onboarding Faster, compliant customer acquisition. Identity, KYC, document workflow, customer data. Digital identity, document AI, exception handling.
Real-time risk and financial crime Lower fraud loss and stronger compliance. Risk 360, transaction events, graph analytics. Alert prioritization, investigator workflow, monitoring.
Open finance platform Embedded finance and partner revenue. API products, consent, partner governance. Developer portal, API gateway, third-party risk controls.
Responsible AI advice Relevant, fair, explainable customer engagement. Customer 360, model governance, advice journeys. Fairness testing, human review, advisor adoption.
### 14.5 Case study structure for publishing 1. **Situation** - OmniCapital serves retail, SME, corporate, insurance, wealth, payments, and markets clients across regulated markets. 2. **Challenge** - It must improve trust, personalization, onboarding, risk controls, resilience, and regulatory transparency. 3. **Transformation approach** - Use Customer 360, open APIs, workflow automation, responsible AI, zero trust, cloud controls, and resilient architecture. 4. **Execution model** - Build data foundations, modernize journeys, strengthen cyber and fraud controls, scale automation, and govern AI. 5. **Value realization** - Measure NPS, onboarding time, cost-to-income, fraud loss, self-service completion, model performance, and compliance. 6. **Long-term capability** - Build a repeatable trusted-finance transformation model across products, channels, risks, and partners. ### 14.6 Alignment rules - **Trust first:** Customer fairness and regulatory accountability guide every decision. - **Data lineage always:** Risk and reporting data must be explainable and auditable. - **Responsible AI by design:** Fairness, explainability, and human accountability are mandatory. - **Resilience by default:** Critical services must be observable, recoverable, and secure. - **Open but governed:** Partner APIs require consent, security, and third-party controls. - **Value after go-live:** Track benefits continuously. ### 14.7 Final aligned positioning ## Aligned case study positioning OmniCapital Financial Group Ltd. demonstrates how financial-services transformation becomes measurable when customer trust, digital journeys, risk intelligence, open APIs, responsible AI, resilience, and value realization are governed as one integrated operating model.
